question.text: Ms. Anjali Menon, asset-allocation head at a family office, is evaluating why Cat III AIFs deserve a strategic allocation alongside listed equity and bonds. Chapter 2, Section 2.5 identifies the PRIMARY portfolio-management rationale for alternatives. Which of the following BEST captures that rationale?

answer.text: Alternatives guarantee higher returns than equities in every cycle and therefore replace equity
Alternatives deliver improved RISK-ADJUSTED returns (alpha) through off-market strategies and provide diversification because of low correlation with traditional assets
Alternatives provide a regulator-guaranteed principal protection that listed markets cannot offer
Alternatives are preferred because they are cheaper and more tax-efficient than mutual funds in every case

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.5 and Table 2.3 identify the primary benefits of alternatives: (i) risk diversification beyond traditional avenues, (ii) better risk-return trade-off, (iii) alpha generation through off-market strategies, and (iv) growth capital to opportunities bank finance will not reach. Section 2.6.1 reinforces that non-traditional assets held by hedge funds have 'low correlations with traditional assets such as equities, fixed income securities and cash,' enabling portfolio diversification. The Trap: Option A is the 'return-chasing' misconception — alternatives carry high risks and may underperform. Option C is regulatorily false. Option D is wrong — Cat III is taxed at fund level at MMR (42.744% for derivatives income after the footnote in Section 2.6.1), often WORSE than mutual funds on tax. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B (Distributors) frame the same rationale for client suitability. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) stresses diversification within listed markets; XIX-E widens the palette to alternatives. Manager's Pro-Tip: At the Cat III desk, 'alpha' must be decomposed into market-timing, factor-tilt, and security-selection components using attribution analytics. If 80% of your excess return is just a cheap beta tilt, you are not delivering real alpha — and investor due-diligence will catch it in a bad quarter.
